data.name: agent
data.shape: Agent — displayName, status, revision, binding, tradingConfig
data.source: app.listAgents.execute, the row matching the route id

data.name: catalog
data.shape: Catalog — undefaultable fields, position-management presets with the platform's own values
data.source: app.readCatalog.execute — BattleGrid's live declaration, never a compiled list

data.name: proposed
data.shape: { consequence, confirmationToken } plus the resolved changes
data.source: app.describeEdit.execute — run only in the review branch, against the values the GET form carried

data.name: query
data.shape: review, problem, displayName, tc.*, pm.*, pmPreset
data.source: searchParams — the GET form navigates back here carrying what was typed

components.purpose: Change what an agent owns, in two requests: a form that asks, then a review that states the consequence before anything is applied.
components.current_implementation: max-w-3xl centered column in the form branch, max-w-2xl in the review branch, space-y-6/4, p-6. The two branches are one route split on ?review=1 — submitting the form is a GET that navigates back here, and this page then proposes the change and renders the consequence the confirmation was issued against. refused-proposal and preset-unresolvable both re-render the form with the reason as its problem banner — but with the agent's current values as defaults, so everything the operator typed is lost (behavior, not styling). catalog-unreadable renders h1 + role=alert reason + a plain underlined link back; no-such-agent renders h1 + underlined link to /agents.
constraints: The two-request split is spec, not layout: 'the consequence is shown and the change is not yet made / it is made only on a further request the user initiated' — openspec/specs/agent-authoring/spec.md:520-523. A design that merges form and confirmation into one submission changes behavior and is requires-spec-change.
The page renders whole from one server round trip — no client JS, no hydration. Every state change is a full navigation.

The form submits by GET and its values ride the query string — spec'd as legitimate at openspec/specs/agent-authoring/spec.md:348-351; a design must not restyle it into something that looks like it acts.

components.purpose: Everything the agent owns on one form — name, money limits, position management — plus an honest note about what is inherited and not editable here.

actions.effect: GET-navigates to the same route with review=1 and every typed value in the query; the next request proposes the change

components.current_implementation: space-y-6 form: name input, MoneyLimits fieldset, PositionManagement section, then two BUTTON_SECONDARY controls ('Review the change' and 'Back to <name>') in flex flex-wrap gap-3 — no mobile full-width stack. Below the form, a 'Not editable here' section renders the binding through the shared components. The not-editable states replace the whole form with a role=alert sentence: archived names reactivation as the way back; platform-locked says BattleGrid does not permit the change.
constraints: 'Review the change' is deliberately BUTTON_SECONDARY, not primary — a method=get form composes a preview and reaches no operation (control.ts's stated rule). The primary in this flow belongs to agent-edit-confirm, one request later.
Inherited configuration MUST stay presented as inherited, not editable — openspec/specs/agent-authoring/spec.md:144-147 ('MUST NOT present strategy-owned configuration as editable from the agent').
An archived agent's refusal must keep naming reactivation as what makes changes possible again — openspec/specs/agent-authoring/spec.md:231-232.
Every control rendered must keep reaching the operation — openspec/specs/agent-authoring/spec.md:326-328; a design may not add a decorative control.

components.purpose: Show the refusal that bounced a submitted edit back to the person who typed it.
components.current_implementation: DT-0004's danger treatment: rounded-gc-2 border-danger-default bg-danger-subtle p-4 text-sm text-text-primary with role=alert — but without the semibold 'Refused:' prefix the archive page's banner carries; here the reason text stands alone.
constraints: role=alert must survive.
The reason shown is the one the operation returned — openspec/specs/agent-authoring/spec.md:474-475; a design must not truncate or paraphrase it.

components.purpose: The six questions BattleGrid will not answer for you — spending limits the platform declines to default, prefilled with the agent's current values.
components.current_implementation: A fieldset wearing the consequence tokens (rounded-gc-2 border-consequence-border bg-consequence-subtle p-4) with a legend and an explanatory paragraph; money fields in a 1-col/sm:2-col grid, each with LABEL, CONTROL, and an aria-describedby hint. Which fields render is driven by undefaultableFields(catalog) — a field the platform starts defaulting stops being asked, with no release. tradingMode renders OFF first and selected, with a stated caveat that APPROVAL_REQUIRED cannot be answered in this product yet.
constraints: Where 0 removes a limit, the warning MUST stay beside the box it is typed into — openspec/specs/agent-authoring/spec.md:366-367 ('Grid-Commander SHALL say so where that value is entered') and :391-394. The strong-tagged sentence inside the hint is that warning.
Current values MUST stay prefilled — openspec/specs/agent-authoring/spec.md:386-389: an empty box submitted is a limit removed, because tradingConfig is all-or-nothing (:370-372).
The hint is wired by aria-describedby — a relayout must keep the association.
Field controls are the shared CONTROL/LABEL constants from control.ts — styling changes go through them, not per-field classNames.

components.purpose: How the agent exits its positions: manage like a catalog preset, or edit the twelve values as CUSTOM — with the truth about the label said first.
components.current_implementation: A section: the drift line first (role=status, rounded-gc-2 border-border-default p-3 — naming the differing fields when the agent's values are not its preset's), then the 'Manage like' select (empty option = leave it alone, presets with 'BattleGrid's own values', CUSTOM last), a semantics paragraph, and the twelve pm.* fields in a 1-col/sm:2-col grid — checkboxes for booleans, number/text inputs otherwise.
constraints: Drift MUST be said, naming the differing fields — openspec/specs/agent-authoring/spec.md:593-596 ('the edit surface MUST say so, naming the differing fields — the label alone is not the truth'). role=status on that line must survive.

The choice semantics are spec: preset sends the platform's values wholesale, CUSTOM sends the fields as edited, no choice sends nothing — openspec/specs/agent-authoring/spec.md:586-590. Copy restating them must not drift from that.
Only presets whose configuration the platform supplied are offered (config !== null) — openspec/specs/agent-authoring/spec.md:548-550.

components.purpose: What the agent is bound to, in words that stay honest when the binding is broken.
components.current_implementation: Shared BindingSummary (binding.tsx), inline text with font-medium on the strategy name or the state word. ORPHANED states only what the payload supports: the strategy can no longer be read, and the revision the configuration came from. An unrecognised state is rendered as the platform's own word, uninterpreted.
constraints: One component for every surface that describes a binding — they drifted once (Volatilis, 2026-08-06) and a design must restyle the shared component, not fork a per-page copy.
The ORPHANED sentence must not gain copy that guesses what the state means — the operational meaning is unestablished and the component says so deliberately.

components.purpose: Where the inherited configuration comes from, and what may honestly be said about it while the binding is not intact.
components.current_implementation: Shared BindingInheritance (binding.tsx), a plain sentence following the summary in the 'Not editable here' section. Bound: changed by editing that strategy or by rebinding. Not intact: names the materialized revision and stops.
constraints: The not-intact sentence deliberately does not offer rebinding as the remedy — that is unestablished, per the backlog item that found it. Copy changes here are behavior.

components.purpose: What the confirmation was issued against, rendered so a person reads it — then one committing button and one visible way out.

actions.effect: POSTs the server action with agentId, confirmationToken, and every proposed value as hidden fields (changes, tc.*, pm.*); success lands on /agents/[id], refusal redirects to the form branch with ?problem=

components.current_implementation: space-y-4 form: h2 'Change <name>?', the consequence block, hidden inputs carrying the token and the resolved values, then BUTTON_PRIMARY 'Apply this to <name>' beside a BUTTON_SECONDARY anchor 'Change something else' in flex flex-wrap gap-3 — no mobile full-width stack.
constraints: The hidden values are the confirmation binding — the token digests the proposed values, so the form must keep exactly one submit path posting exactly what was proposed (openspec/specs/agent-authoring/spec.md:507-518).
Cancel must remain a visible peer of the submit, never a text link beneath it (DT-0002 ruling, restated in control.ts).
Deliberately NOT danger-styled — DT-0002: the weight belongs on the consequence block, not the button.

components.purpose: State what applying this edit does, in the sentence the token was issued against, before the button that does it.
components.current_implementation: rounded-gc-2 border-consequence-border p-4 text-sm with role=alert — the consequence border token but no bg-consequence-subtle fill, so it sits lighter than the archive page's fully-tinted callout.
constraints: The text is the same string stored with the token — a design must not paraphrase, truncate, or summarize it (openspec/specs/agent-authoring/spec.md:526-527: 'the sentence recorded is the sentence the user was shown').
Consequence outranks everything on a screen (system.json principle) — this block must not become lighter than the buttons below it.
role=alert must survive.

components.purpose: Tell an editor whose agent did not load whether to wait or to reconnect — and that their work is not gone.
components.current_implementation: Shared WhyNotLoaded (why-not-loaded.tsx), a plain mt-2 paragraph under the roster-unreadable heading. Two sentences, chosen by cause: BattleGrid refused the authority, or could not be reached.
constraints: The refused/unreachable distinction is spec — openspec/specs/agent-authoring/spec.md:20-24: telling a user 'could not be reached' when the platform refused sends them to wait for an outage that is not happening. A design must keep the two texts distinct.
The reassurance ('does not mean … gone') is the point of the sentence and must survive any rewording — openspec/specs/agent-authoring/spec.md:40.

components.current_implementation: BUTTON_PRIMARY constant from control.ts — accent.default bg, min-h-control (44px, DT-0003's token), rounded-gc-2, hover to accent.hover over duration-fast, active holds hover at duration-instant. No pending/loading state between click and redirect.
constraints: Styling changes go through the BUTTON_PRIMARY constant in control.ts, shared by every committing submit in the product — not a per-page className.
Not danger-styled — DT-0002's ruling, restated in control.ts.
44px minimum tap target (system.json principle).
Focus ring comes from the one global rule in globals.css — do not add a per-element ring.

components.purpose: The peers and the asks: 'Review the change' (a GET submit that only composes), 'Back to <name>', and 'Change something else'.

actions.effect: The anchors return to /agents/[id] or /agents/[id]/edit without applying anything; the GET submit navigates into the review branch

components.current_implementation: BUTTON_SECONDARY constant from control.ts — inline-flex centering, min-h-control, bordered, DT-0004's hover (border-strong + bg-sunken over duration-fast). Worn by both a submit button (the GET form) and anchors on this route.
constraints: The cancel anchors must remain anchors (pure navigation, no form participation) and visible peers of their submit.
Styling changes go through the BUTTON_SECONDARY constant in control.ts.
44px minimum tap target (system.json principle).

components.purpose: Turn away a request without authority, with the one remedy that works: connect.
components.current_implementation: Shared NotConnected component (require-connection.tsx): h1 + message, and since DT-0006 the connect link is an anchor wearing BUTTON_SECONDARY — the way in as a target, not a sentence, at the 44px floor with secondary's hover. Used by every authenticated page, so this treatment is inherited everywhere.
constraints: Every no-authority cause renders this same page by design (see design W-C) — a design must not invent per-cause variants.

flows.name: Edit an agent
steps: change name, money limits, or position management
submit 'Review the change' — a GET carrying every value
read the consequence the token was issued against
land on /agents/[id] with the change made

flows.name: The edit is refused after apply
steps: platform or product refuses (rejected fields, invalid values, revision moved)
redirected back to the form branch with ?problem=
problem banner states every reason above a fresh form (typed values are not restored)

flows.name: The proposal itself is refused
steps: describeEdit refuses a field or the preset cannot be resolved
the form re-renders with the reason as its problem banner, defaults back to current values

flows.name: Walk away
steps: back on the agent or the form, nothing changed

accessibility.notes: Problem and consequence blocks and the not-editable refusals carry role=alert; the position drift line carries role=status. Money hints are associated via aria-describedby. Focus ring is global (focus-visible, 2px). No client JS: every state change is a full navigation.
